abstract.p: Question-Answering (QA) systems are vital for rapidly accessing and comprehending information in academic literature. However, some academic questions require synthesizing information across multiple documents. While several prior resources consider multi-document QA, they often do not strictly enforce crossdocument synthesis or exploit the explicit interpaper structure that links sources. To address this, we introduce a pipeline methodology for constructing a Multi-Document Academic QA (MDA-QA) dataset. By both detecting communities based on citation networks and leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), we were able to form thematically coherent communities and generate QA pairs related to multidocument content automatically. We further develop an automated filtering mechanism to ensure multi-document dependence. Our resulting dataset consists of 6,804 QA pairs and serves as a benchmark for evaluating multidocument retrieval and QA systems. Our experimental results highlight that standard lexical and embedding-based retrieval methods struggle to locate all relevant documents, indicating a persistent gap in multi-document reasoning. We release our dataset and source code for the community. 1
